Follow-up call to confirm network/VPC peering requirements

Anya: Draft perf benchmark plan and example infra config by 2026-06-29

summary: Initial discovery for migration from OpenAI hosted API to Redwood Dedicated. Customer is healthcare-focused, concerned about PHI, latency and cost. Primary drivers: data residency, FIPS/KMS, predictable throughput for peak hours. Redwood AE+SE reviewed hosting options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), discussed compatibility, eval parity with their current OpenAI flows, and proposed a Dedicated pilot and perf benchmark.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-06-25
Time: 10:00am PT / 17:00Z
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Anya Kuznetsova (Redwood SE), Liam O'Rourke (Redwood CSM), Maya Chen (CTO - Nebula), Rajiv Singh (DevOps), Elena Morales (ML Lead), Priya Kapoor (Security)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you taking the time. quick intro - i'm samir, i'm the AE working with nebula. we have anya from our se team and liam from customer success. how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Maya: good, thanks. excited to dig in. little background - we're a healthcare startup, we run clinical summarization and triage models, currently on OpenAI API. latency's getting rough during peak clinic hours and cost is spiking since we ramped usage.
[00:28] Samir: appreciated. can you run through current stack and scale?
[00:33] Elena: sure, we have a preprocessing pipeline in GKE, we call OpenAI completions and chat endpoints for summarization and triage. about 300k tokens/day average, spikes to 1.2M tokens on Mondays; 99th perc latency around 1.1s per token - which adds up.
[00:47] Rajiv: infra-wise we use Azure for most services, but the model calls are directly to OpenAI. networking is standard, no VPC peering currently - we wanted to discuss options for private peering because of PHI.
[01:02] Priya: security is the big one for us - PHI, audits coming up Q3. we need SOC 2 plus evidence of encryption at rest with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and audit logs for all inference requests.
[01:15] Anya: absolutely, that's a common pattern. Redwood supports Dedicated and Private deployments; Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools with isolation and optional VPC peering and customer-managed KMS. quick question - are you leaning toward a managed hosted approach or fully private?
[01:31] Maya: prefer Dedicated or Private. hosted is attractive for speed to market but compliance and residency push us away. cost also matters - we want predictable monthly spend rather than variable.
[01:42] Samir: makes sense. quick qual - what's your timeline and success criteria for migration?
[01:48] Elena: timeline's target for pilot in Q3, production by Q4. success criteria: parity in summarization quality (no regression on clinical accuracy), 20-30% reduction in per-token cost, and 95th perc latency below current peaks.
[02:02] Anya: great, those are actionable. on quality parity - can you describe your eval setup? do you have prompt sets and reference outputs?
[02:09] Elena: yes, we have a labeled set of about 5k clinical notes and a scoring harness. currently running on GPT-4o-ish endpoint (they call it internally), but we use a mix of Llama-based + OpenAI checkpoints. we need to ensure Redwood can host open models or compatible endpoints without changing the prompt engineering significantly.
[02:30] Samir: Redwood's model catalog includes curated open models and we support multiple runtime options. compatibility is usually about tokenizer differences and sometimes sampling defaults. we can run evals on your prompt set to measure parity; our SEs usually run a small A/B with exact prompts.
[02:45] Rajiv: about runtime - we've heard about vLLM and TGI, are those relevant? will our code need rework?
[02:52] Anya: good question. vLLM and TGI are runtimes; Redwood's Dedicated runtime is independent but supports loading models that are typically run on vLLM/TGI. for customers, the API surface can stay the same - we map your calls (chat/completions) to the serving runtime. some edge cases with streaming semantics or function-calling require small changes but nothing drastic.
[03:12] Maya: streaming semantics - we rely on token-level streaming for UI responsiveness. any differences there?
[03:18] Anya: we support streaming and still preserve chunking semantics. occasional differences in the way stop tokens are handled can surface; we include those in the eval plan.
[03:26] Priya: about encryption - do you support customer-managed keys? FIPS? HSM?
[03:31] Samir: yes, Dedicated can integrate with customer KMS/HSM, we have a checklist for FIPS requirements - for Private deployments we can support strict FIPS stacks. we will share SOC2 and KMS documentation after the call.
[03:44] Rajiv: network wise - will we need to open egress to Redwood's host, or can we do VPC peering?
[03:50] Anya: Dedicated supports VPC peering and private link options; we can do peering into your Azure VNet, or set up a private endpoint. we'll capture the exact network port requirements in the follow-up doc.
[04:02] Elena: perf - you mentioned kernel selection and batching. our main concern is latency at tail when we batch. can you preserve low latency for single-requests while amortizing cost?
[04:12] Anya: yes, our serving runtime supports smart routing and workload-aware batching. we can pin some capacity for low-latency paths and use batching for background workloads. for Dedicated we can expose autoscaling policies and burst capacity.
[04:26] Maya: any hard guarantees on 95th perc?
[04:29] Samir: for Dedicated we offer SLA-backed targets and can commit to latency SLOs in the enterprise contract; during a pilot we can instrument and share token-level latency breakdowns.
[04:40] Rajiv: cost - we've seen big variance between OpenAI and self-hosted. what's the expectation on per-token cost if we move to Dedicated?
[04:49] Samir: depends on model and quantization. in many cases customers see 20-40% unit cost reduction with Dedicated plus batching and KV caching; we'll estimate after we run your workload profile.
[04:58] Elena: are there any modeling changes required? e.g., do we need to quantize or change to a different architecture?
[05:03] Anya: often we recommend quantization for cost, but we only do that after evals to ensure quality parity. we also recommend model candidate suggestions - some customers move to a slightly smaller model with negligible quality loss.
[05:18] Priya: audit logs - do you log request/response content? we need to show auditability but also control PHI exposure in logs.
[05:25] Samir: audit logs are configurable; for PHI you can opt out of storing full payloads, and we support redaction and request-level logging of metadata. we'll include the audit log retention options in the security pack.
[05:38] Maya: ok sounds good. whats the typical pilot shape? we want a 1-2 week pilot using our 50-100 prompts to validate latency and quality.
[05:46] Anya: typical pilot: we provision a small Dedicated cluster, run your prompt set through both OpenAI and Redwood for A/B, collect metrics (latency, token cost, quality scores). we also do a run with burst patterns to simulate peak. we can do that next week if you can share prompts.
[06:00] Rajiv: timing - we need network approvals but could probably get it in a week.
[06:04] Samir: excellent. i'll send the pricing and the pilot runbook after this call. anya will follow up with perf plan and the exact infra reqs.
[06:12] Liam: i'll loop in CSM to kick off onboarding and make sure the trial support tickets are routed.
[06:18] Elena: quick note - we also do internal evals with a proprietary scoring script; we'll share results and would like Redwood to run the same script for parity.
[06:26] Anya: absolutely, if you send the harness we'll run it.
[06:30] Priya: one last question - competitors: we've talked to Anthropic about their private deployment and Azure is expensive. how is Redwood different from Anthropic's private offering?
[06:40] Samir: good question - differentiation is in the developer and ops experience: unified API across hosted/dedicated/private, stronger observability (token-level costs, per-route dashboards), and built-in rollback/fallback policies. we also focus on inference economics - batching, KV caching, quantization recommendations.
[06:58] Maya: ok that's helpful.
[07:00] Samir: recap and next steps: i'll send pricing + sizing, SOC2 + KMS docs, and a pilot runbook; anya will send perf benchmark plan; you (nebula) will share prompt set, evaluation harness, and security constraints. we'll aim to start pilot next week pending network approvals. any other open items?
[07:18] Maya: no, that's it. thanks everyone.
[07:22] Rajiv: thank you.
[07:24] Samir: great, appreciate your time. we'll follow up via email and schedule the pilot kick-off.

Notes about transcription quality: occasional word swaps (e.g., "FIPS" transcribed as "fips"), speaker attribution occasionally simplified to roles.
notes: Pilot requested: 1-week Dedicated pilot, 50-100 prompt A/B, customer to share harness and prompts; Redwood to run parity eval and provide per-token latency/cost breakdown.
